commitResults.messageTitle: Move Java classes into the alpha package
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha and Task use the default package, which makes the source layout
less clear and does not follow the project's Java coding standard.

Move both classes into the alpha package and align their documentation,
parameter names, and whitespace with the standard. Update the README
launch path so setup instructions continue to point to the application
entry point.

Tasks only store descriptions and completion state, so the chatbot
cannot distinguish todos, deadlines, or events.

Add commands to create each task type and store its relevant date and
time details. Format list entries with type markers and scheduling
information so users can distinguish tasks at a glance.

Task type data and formatting are handled in one Task class, coupling
unrelated fields and behavior.

Introduce Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses that extend Task and
override toString for type-specific display. Continue storing them in a
Task array so common operations rely on polymorphism.

Alpha.main handles both the application lifecycle and every non-exit
command. This makes the entry point longer than the recommended size
and hides its high-level control flow among command-specific details.

Extract the command dispatch into processCommand and return the updated
task count explicitly. This keeps state changes visible without adding
shared mutable state, while allowing main to read as a short sequence of
startup, input, dispatch, and exit steps.

Restore the class header Javadoc and normalize array creation spacing
so the touched file follows the project Java coding standard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add error handling for invalid user input
Refactor error handling to use exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Error handling currently prints messages directly at each error site,
which spreads output formatting across the codebase and makes it hard
to keep the bot's tone consistent. This becomes unwieldy as new
commands and error cases are added.

Add a custom AlphaException class to represent chatbot-specific
errors, and rework every error site to throw it instead of printing.
The main loop catches the exception and reports it through one shared
helper, keeping output formatting in a single place.

Aligned all error messages to end with "..." to match the bot's style,
including the mark and unmark messages that previously ended with a
period. Simplified parseIndex to return a primitive int now that it
throws on invalid input, removing the earlier null-return handling.

All classes currently live flat in the alpha package, which mixes the
task data model with the application logic. As the chatbot grows, this
makes the code harder to navigate and new responsibilities harder to
place.

Move the task model classes Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event into a new
alpha.task package, keeping the source root at src/main/java. Alpha and
AlphaException remain in the root alpha package, since they serve the
whole application. Add explicit imports for the task classes in Alpha
instead of relying on package-local access.

Tasks can be added and marked, but cannot be removed from the list.

Add the delete command with task-number validation and a confirmation
showing the removed task and remaining count. Preserve task order and
reuse the freed array slot for future additions.

The fixed task array limits the list to 100 tasks and requires manual
counting and shifting during deletion.

Use an ArrayList to grow the list as needed and let the collection
manage its size and removals. Preserve task ordering, command output,
and input validation.

The test plan defines a workflow but contains no executable cases.

Add 11 cases with complete input and expected output for task commands,
invalid-input recovery, deletion boundaries, and collection growth.
Clarify encoding, whitespace, failure handling, and session records to
make future runs repeatable. Mark all cases as not run and distinguish
parser compatibility checks from new acceptance requirements.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save and restore tasks for Level 7
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks disappear when Alpha exits because the list exists only in memory.

Save task changes automatically and restore them on startup using a
relative, platform-independent path. Validate snapshots, import the
legacy format, and preserve data on malformed input or failed saves.
Use atomic replacement and conflict checks to protect existing files.

Document the storage behavior and add a repeatable UI test runner.
Compile with Java 25.0.3 and pass all 10 UI cases in Linux/WSL, including
first-run folder creation and corrupted-file preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Gradle support for executable fat JARs
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the Gradle wrapper and configure Shadow to package Alpha with its
runtime dependencies. Select Java 25 and the alpha.Alpha entry point,
and document how to build and run the artifact.

Verify the build and a standalone launch with Java 25.0.3 in WSL.
Keep generated JARs excluded from version control.

Integrate task deletion and collection-based task storage while
preserving the independent Level-6 branch history.

Integrate persistence and fat-JAR support with the independently
developed deletion and Collections extension.

Resolve command-handler and test-plan conflicts using ArrayList task
storage. Save deletions with rollback on failure, retain unlimited task
counts within the snapshot size limit, and combine both UI suites.

Pass all 23 UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL and rebuild and launch the
fat JAR successfully. Keep generated application binaries out of Git.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks in a human-readable format
commitResults.messageBody:
Base64 task fields make saved data difficult to read and inspect.

Store new saves as readable text with escaped special characters.
Keep support for existing encoded and legacy files, converting them
on the next successful task change to preserve existing tasks.

Document the format and update UI fixtures and console records.
All 25 UI tests pass, and the rebuilt fat JAR launches successfully.

Alpha mixes console input and response formatting with command handling
and persistence. This makes display changes touch the same class as
changes to task behavior.

Extract command reading, greetings, dividers, lists, confirmations, and
error display into Ui. Let each Alpha instance own Ui and Storage, with
main delegating to run. Keep command parsing and task mutations in Alpha
for later increments so this extraction stays independently reviewable.

Preserve exact console output, EOF and bye behavior, startup error
handling, and confirmation only after successful saves. Rename the
addition helper to saveAddition to reflect its remaining responsibility.

Validate with all 25 existing UI cases using Java 25.0.3 in WSL, checking
exact output and existing file checkpoints. Refresh the test session
record without changing expected outputs or storage behavior.

Alpha combines input syntax rules with task mutations and persistence.
This makes changes to command parsing touch unrelated application logic.

Move command recognition, task construction, and task-number validation
into Parser. Return a command type, a new task, or a validated index
without printing output, changing the list, or accessing storage.
Keep operation dispatch, rollback, and save coordination in Alpha so
this increment remains focused and independently reviewable.

Preserve exact command matching, whitespace rules, missing time fields,
error messages, and exit behavior. Use a small command-type enum instead
of introducing a separate class for every command.

Run all 25 existing UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL. All pass with
unchanged expected console output and file checkpoints. Refresh the
complete test session record.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task collection operations into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha directly manages an ArrayList and changes task completion state.
This couples application coordination to collection operations.

Introduce TaskList to own the ordered collection and provide add,
delete, insert, mark, unmark, and status operations. Copy the restored
collection on construction and provide shallow collection copies for
display and storage so callers cannot modify the internal list structure.
Task objects remain shared; this does not introduce deep immutability.

Keep save coordination and rollback in Alpha, restoring deleted tasks
at their original position and preserving prior completion states on
failure. Leave file handling and command syntax unchanged.

Run all 25 UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL and refresh the session
record. Exact console output and file checkpoints pass unchanged.
Save-failure rollback remains outside the existing UI test coverage.
This completes the requested Ui, Parser, Storage, and TaskList split.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract additions into an executable command
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha coordinates every operation directly, which keeps command-specific
behavior in the application class after parsing has been extracted.

Introduce an abstract Command with execute and a default non-exit flag.
Move the addition workflow into AddCommand, shared by todos, deadlines,
and events. Accept a parsed task and handle append, save, rollback on
failure, and confirmation after success in the command itself.

Execute additions through the Command abstraction in Alpha. Keep other
operations and parser dispatch in place for subsequent small increments.
This establishes the command hierarchy without changing user syntax or
introducing separate addition classes with identical behavior.

Run all 25 existing UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL; all pass with
unchanged expected output and file checkpoints. Refresh the complete
session record. Save-failure rollback is outside this suite's coverage.

Alpha still contains deletion and completion-status workflows despite
using a command abstraction for additions. These operation details obscure
its application-coordination role.

Move the existing operation bodies into DeleteCommand, MarkCommand, and
UnmarkCommand, each extending Command and accepting a validated index.
Keep mutation, saving, rollback, and confirmation together in each class.
Preserve deletion order and prior completion status when saving fails.

Use one execute call for all task-changing commands in Alpha. Retain
similar mark and unmark implementations to keep this extraction focused.
Leave list, exit, and parser-driven command creation for the next step.

Run all 25 existing UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL and refresh the
session record. Expected output and file checkpoints pass unchanged.
The suite does not cover save-failure rollback; those bodies were moved
without changing their behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Run parsed commands through a uniform loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Alpha still constructs concrete commands and handles list and exit
separately. This leaves command-specific dispatch in the main class.

Add ListCommand and ExitCommand, and let Parser.parse create every
supported command. Make the command type and parsing helpers private;
construct addition commands directly without recognizing the input twice.
Pass the current task count to preserve validation before execution.

Replace Alpha's dispatch helper with parse, execute, and isExit calls.
Retain EOF handling and print one divider in finally after each response.
List and exit remain read-only, and bye still ignores subsequent input.
Commands are parsed and immediately executed against the same task list.

Run all 25 existing UI cases with Java 25.0.3 in WSL and refresh the
session record. Exact output and file checkpoints pass unchanged,
including exit, EOF, invalid-command recovery, and persistence cases.
This completes the requested command hierarchy and uniform main loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse and persist deadline dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline fields are stored as arbitrary strings, so Alpha cannot validate
calendar dates or distinguish meaningful deadline times.

Store deadlines as LocalDateTime and retain whether a time was supplied.
Accept ISO dates and day-first slash dates with optional HHmm or HH:mm
times. Display English month names and reject impossible dates and times.
Preserve explicit midnight separately from date-only deadlines.

Save ISO date or datetime values and restore them without losing time
information. Report invalid saved deadlines with their line number and
preserve the original file rather than guessing dates for legacy text.
Document accepted formats and the migration needed for free-text dates.

Update deadline fixtures and add validation and persistence cases.
All 32 UI tests pass with Java 25.0.3 in WSL, including leap days,
invalid times, midnight, reloads, and rejected-input file preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add deadline queries by calendar date
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline dates are typed values, but users must inspect the entire list
to find tasks due on a particular day.

Add a read-only on command accepting ISO or day-first slash dates.
Match completed and incomplete deadlines by calendar date, regardless
of time, and preserve original list order and task numbers. Display an
explicit message when no deadlines match. Exclude todos and events,
whose time fields remain free text.

Keep parsing in Parser, date matching in TaskList, and presentation in
Ui through OnCommand. Document the syntax and read-only behavior.

Run all 35 UI tests with Java 25.0.3 in WSL. New cases cover date
boundaries, retained task numbers, invalid queries, fresh storage,
file preservation, and results after task changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword searches for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users must scan the full task list to find descriptions containing a
particular word or phrase.

Add a read-only find command using case-insensitive literal substring
matching across all task types and completion states. Search descriptions
only, preserve original task numbers, reject blank keywords, and display
an explicit empty result. Keep search results usable with mark and delete.

Implement parsing, matching, and display in their existing responsible
classes through FindCommand. Document phrase matching and file-preserving
behavior.

Run all 37 UI tests with Java 25.0.3 in WSL. New cases cover mixed task
types, case, phrases, Unicode, literal punctuation, excluded time fields,
invalid input, original numbering, changes after deletion, and unchanged
save files. Retain the complete test session record.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete Javadoc coverage for application code
commitResults.messageBody:
Some getters, command overrides, and storage helpers lack explicit
Javadoc, leaving behavior and caller expectations undocumented.

Add the missing headers and clarify shared task references, date-only
midnight values, free-text event fields, and read-only command behavior.
Document storage decoding and error handling without changing code.

Verify Javadoc headers for all 107 explicit class, enum, method, and
constructor declarations. Generate documentation with Java 25 doclint
and warnings as errors, excluding missing-tag lint. Confirm executable
tokens are unchanged across all 19 Java source files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the Alpha user guide for GitHub Pages
commitResults.messageBody:
The documentation directory contains placeholder sections, leaving users
without a complete guide to starting Alpha and managing their tasks.

Replace the template with a concise guide covering setup, all commands,
date and time formats, task numbering, saving, and common errors. Keep
examples aligned with the supported deadline and search behavior.

Configure the Primer theme and publish the guide at the site root from
the docs directory. The Pages repository setting and live rendering still
need verification after publication.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review feedback on UI indentation
commitResults.messageBody:
Console messages embed layout spaces, while the banner and greeting
lack the indentation used by other responses.

Centralize output formatting in printMessage with named indentation
constants. Align the banner and greeting with standard messages while
preserving distinct divider and task-detail indentation.

Address SanchitGarg08's indentation review on PR #76. The related
reviews about main-method responsibilities, package declarations, and
hardcoded task-index offsets are already resolved by earlier changes.

Update expected console output and record all 37 UI tests passing
with Java 25.0.3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve date input guidance for Level 8
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline errors omit supported input formats, and date queries do not
explain that a time must be omitted.

List all supported deadline formats and valid 24-hour time ranges.
Give date queries a concrete example and date-only guidance, using a
shared error message for malformed and impossible dates.

Update expected output and record all 37 UI tests passing on Java 25.
This is a follow-up to the Level-8 implementation already on master.
Improve date input guidance for Level 8

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve guidance for searches without results
commitResults.messageBody:
Search output gives the same response for an empty task list and for
existing tasks that do not match, leaving users without a next step.

Distinguish an empty list and suggest adding a task with an example.
For unmatched descriptions, suggest a shorter keyword or the list
command. Preserve matching behavior and original task numbering.

Update expected output and record all 37 UI tests passing on Java 25.
This follows up on the Level-9 implementation already on master.
Improve guidance for searches without results

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct outdated README descriptions and examples
commitResults.messageBody:
The README still describes a template and shows outdated startup,
farewell, and empty-search output.

Describe Alpha as a task manager and link to its User Guide. Match the
examples to current UI indentation, separate startup from explicit
exit, and document both empty-list and unmatched-search guidance.
Correct the IntelliJ IDEA naming throughout the setup instructions.

Validate the examples against the current UI and run git diff --check.
No application code changes; no additional test run is needed.
